title: v1/chat.completions: introduce stop-weighting, preserve toolcall role args, and deterministic logprob envelope for framed streaming
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Add v1/chat.completions parameter mapping: stop_weighting, preserve toolcall arguments for role/tool handoff, and a deterministic framed logprob envelope for streaming consumers. Backwards-compatible behavior preserved for existing clients. Includes tests and compatibility shims.
description: Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported subtle regressions when combining stop arrays with streaming and tool/function calls. Specifically: (1) no way to express relative stop importance (we had only boolean stops), (2) toolcall argument/role metadata lost when intermediary framing happened, and (3) streaming consumers observed non-deterministic logprob attachments when fragments were reassembled. This PR implements a minimal, backward-compatible extension to address these gaps. Design summary: - stop_weighting param: allow an optional numeric weight per stop token or sequence. The field is an array matching stops semantics: when provided, runtime uses weighted-stop arbitration instead of first-match-only. Defaults to uniform weights to preserve existing behavior. - toolcall-preserve: ensure the tool/function call envelope preserves role and argument metadata across stream fragmenting/reassembly. This required threading a small immutable metadata header through the stream coordinator and adding a stable boundary marker so tools can resume. - framed-logprob-envelope: coined a compact logprob envelope that is emitted only when the streaming frame is closed (or when a heartbeat indicates finality). Logprobs are now deterministic by construction (we serialize sorted token indices and a base64 payload) which eliminates assembly race conditions. Implementation highlights: - API adapter: v1 compatibility adapter now accepts stop_weighting (v1 -> internal mapping stop_weights[]) and normalizes numeric strings to floats. Old clients that send only stop are unaffected. - Serving runtime: added weighted-stop comparator that can be pluggable in the step loop; microbenchmarked to <2% p99 delta at typical batch sizes. - Stream coordinator: added a lightweight frame header (0xFA marker + 3-byte version) and a finalization heartbeat for long-running streams. - Toolcall handoff: preserved tool role/args in the tool-metadata header and added a reconcile step in the response-synthesizer so downstream SDKs receive the original call payload. - Tests: unit tests for the comparator, integration tests covering streaming frames with simulated packet reordering, and an end-to-end suite verifying v1 clients with/without stop_weighting. Commits: - a1b2c3d: adapter: accept stop_weighting (parse and normalize) - e4f5g6h: runtime: weighted-stop comparator and tests - i7j8k9l: streaming: frame header and heartbeat, stable logprob envelope - m0n1o2p: tooling: preserve toolcall metadata through frames - q3r4s5t: tests: add integration flakiness harness and docs Changes (high level, not exhaustive): - src/compat/v1/adapter.go: add parsing/validation for stop_weighting; map into internal StopPolicy - runtime/stop_policy.go: new weighted comparator implementation - runtime/stop_policy_test.go: unit coverage with many edge cases - services/stream/coordinator.go: attach frame header, heartbeat, and finalization path - services/stream/logprob_envelope.go: compose deterministic logprob blob, base64 serialize - services/tool/handshake.go: persist toolcall role/arg metadata and reconcile on reassembly - docs/openapi/v1_chat.yaml: document stop_weighting field and compatibility notes Small illustrative snippet (compat adapter normalization): "if len(req.StopWeighting) > 0 { for i, w := range req.StopWeighting { req.StopWeights[i] = parseFloat(w) } }" Review conversation (excerpt): - Marta Li (reviewer): "Please validate that empty/partial weight arrays fall back to uniform behavior and add a test for mismatched lengths vs stops." - Aisha Kumar (author): "Added validation to adapter.go to reject mismatched lengths with a clear 400 and unit tests covering mismatches; fallback semantics now documented." - Jared Simms: "Can we avoid copying the full tool payload in the hot path? Concern about extra allocations." - Aisha Kumar: "We store a small immutable reference header (<=256 bytes) on the coordinator hot path and only materialize the full payload when a tool handshake is invoked; benchmark attached." - Omid Rezai: "CI failed once on streaming_reassembly_test previously; make sure the flakiness harness is deterministic." - Aisha Kumar: "Fixed a race in test harness by seeding the reorder RNG and added an assertion to ensure consistent ordering when replayed." CI and validation: - Initial CI run: lint passed, unit tests passed, streaming_integration flaky (1/3 failures) due to test harness race. - After fix: all checks green. Key checks: go-lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-streaming (pass), e2e-compat (pass). Performance: - Microbenchmarks show weighted-stop comparator adds ~0.6% median CPU cost in hot path and p99 <2% on our benchmark cluster (N=16 GPUs, batch size 8). - Streaming latency unaffected for normal frames; small extra bytes for headers (~32B/frame). Backwards-compatibility and migration notes: - Existing clients that omit stop_weighting will behave identically. - Clients that send stop_weighting with fewer weights than stops will receive 400 with explanation. - The API docs include example mappings for common stop-weight heuristics (prefix vs suffix priority). Release/merge notes: - Merged to main via squash by Marta Li on 2026-02-16 after approvals from all reviewers. - Feature guarded behind a v1-compat flag for gradual rollout; dashboard alerts added to watch for error-rate or latency changes. Follow-ups (future work): - Expose a higher-level SDK helper to generate stop weights from prompt-level heuristics. - Consider a compact binary framing option for very high-throughput streaming. - Add a telemetry tag to correlate stop_weighting usage with cost/latency. Related: ENG-1472 (stop arbitration), ENG-1499 (stream reassembly determinism), SUP-822 (customer ticket describing regression).
